texts.preamble: Sathanantham vs The Ii Class Executive Magistrate-Cum on 16 August, 2023 Author: D.Nagarjun Bench: D.Nagarjun Crl.O.P.(MD) Before The Madurai Bench Of Madras High Court Reserved on 20/9/2023 Delivered on 29/9/2023 Coram: The Honourable Dr.Justice D.Nagarjun Crl.O.P.(MD) No.16287 of 2023 and Crl.M.P(MD)Nos.12977 & 12978 of 2023 Sathanantham ... Petitione Vs. 1.The Ii Class Executive Magistrate-cum- The Tahsildar, Paramakudi, Ramanathapuram District. 2.The State rep. by The Inspector of Police (Law & Order), Emaneshwaram Police Station, Ramanathapuram District. ...Respondent Prayer :
texts.facts: It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that the second respondent / the Inspector of Police (Law & Order), Emaneshwaram Police Station, Ramanathapuram District, has submitted a report to the II Class Executive Magistrate-cum-the Tahsildar, Paramakudi / first respondent herein by registering LIR No.47 of 2023 dated 7/8/2023 under Section 110 of Cr.P.C., basing on which, first respondent has issued summons to the petitioner after registering the same as M.C.No.173 of 2023 dated 6/8/2023, asking the petitioner to appear before first respondent on 29/8/2023. It is submitted that the petitioner is not served with the copy of the report including the substance of information. Respondent No.1 has mechanically issued the summons to the petitioner in printed format and the first respondent has not recorded subjective satisfaction prior to issuance of summons.
texts.arguments: The Honble Supreme Court of India in the case of Gopalanachari v. State of Kerala, reported in 1980 (Supp) SCC 649. The relevant paragraphs read as under:- "The constitutional survival of Section 110 certainly depends on its obedience to Article 21, as this Court has expounded. Words of wide import, vague amplitude and far too generalised to be safe in the hands of the Police cannot be constitutionalised in the context of Article 21 unless read down to be as a fair and reasonable legislation with reverence for human rights. A glance at Section 110 shows that only a narrow signification can be attached to the words in clauses (a) to (g), "by habit a robber....", "by habit a receiver of stolen property....", "habitually protects or harbours thieve....", "habitually commits or attempts to commit or abets the commission of .... ", "is so desperate and dangerous as to render his being at large without security hazardous to the community".
